title: Irish Stew
subtitle: Lamb neck braised with potato, onion, and thyme
excerpt: Lamb neck chops layered with sliced potato and onion, simmered in a light stock until the lamb is falling off the bone and the potato has thickened the broth.

recipe.sourceNotes: Irish stew is one of the oldest and most frugal of the traditional Irish dishes, historically made with whatever was available. The classic combination of lamb (or mutton in older recipes), potato, and onion reflects the Irish landscape where sheep grazed the hillsides and potatoes were the staple crop. The dish is deliberately plain: no tomatoes, no wine, no browning of the meat. The potato dissolves into the broth as it cooks, thickening it naturally. Carrot is disputed — some Irish cooks add it, others insist it is inauthentic. This recipe includes it for sweetness.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy-based pot with a lid.

content.text: Unlike most stews, Irish stew does not require browning the meat first: the broth is deliberately pale and light. Layer the potato at the bottom where it will cook down and thicken the stew, and on top where it will absorb the stock and give a more solid layer. Simmer very gently: a hard boil will make the lamb tough. Serve with soda bread.

items.preparation: chops, or neck fillet cut into large chunks

content.text: Layer a third of the potatoes in the base of a large pot. Add all the lamb, onion, and carrot. Season. Tuck in the thyme and bay leaves. Layer the remaining potatoes on top.
Pour over the stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours until the lamb is falling off the bone.
Skim any excess fat from the surface. Discard the thyme and bay leaves. Check seasoning. Scatter with parsley and serve in deep bowls with soda bread.
